title: Quantile‑Hedging Shelf Admission: KV signal fusion for tail-safe micro-batching under sustained QPS
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS with many small requests we observe repeated tail-latency spikes and kv cache churn. Existing admission uses fixed thresholds and headroom heuristics that either over-eject requests (hurting throughput) or let occasional tails blow SLOs. This ticket explores a hybrid admission mechanism — 'quantile‑hedging shelf admission' — that fuses per-tenant KV hotness signals, GPU memory pressure, and recent-percentile latency estimates to make probabilistic slot-grant decisions. The aim is to reduce 99.9th percentile latency regressions at production QPS while preserving median throughput and amortized token cost.

Scope: prototype admission controller in the inference gateway and a lightweight runtime signal exporter. Deliverables: design doc, simulation harness, A/B in canary fleet, rollout + rollback plan, dashboard panels for new signals.

Context: This complements prefix caching improvements in ENG-9214 and microslot eviction work in ENG-8532 but uses a decision layer upstream of the allocator to soften bursts without aggressive KV eviction.

Why unique: Rather than global static headroom or single-signal gating, we compute a rolling conditional quantile of recent token latencies conditioned on KV hit-rate, GPU memutil, and microbatch occupancy, and use that to hedge slot grants probabilistically (shelfing low-probability requests for up to a configured grace window).
acceptance_criteria: Prototype admission controller deployed to canary nodes accepting a feature flag
Simulated workload shows >= 40% reduction in 99.9p tail latency for high-churn KV patterns vs baseline (same median)
End-to-end dashboard with new signals (kv_hit_rate, shelf_queue_length, hedged_grants_ratio, gpu_memutil) in console-2026.03
Automated e2e test that injects KV-hotspot and verifies graceful degrade without >2% drop in overall tokens/sec
Runbook and rollback steps documented and verified with SRE
implementation_notes: Signal inputs: 30s rolling window percentiles for per-tenant token latency (p50, p90, p99, p999), kv_hit_rate sampled per-shard, gpu_memutil (per-GPU), microbatch occupancy histogram

Compute: quantile conditioning implemented in Rust component inside gateway to avoid Python GC jitter; algorithm approximates conditional quantiles using reservoir sketches and light-weight copulas to fuse signals

Decision: each incoming request gets a hedged_score = f(q_p99 | kv_hit_rate, memutil, occupancy) mapped to a shelf probability p_shelf. p_shelf grows with estimated tail risk and recent shelf pressure; if shelved, request held for up to grace_ms (default 12ms) then retried for grant or spilled to lower-cost model variant
KV coordination: add a small kv_hotness token to request metadata so downstream runtime can bias cache retention; does NOT require global locks
Backpressure integration: the hedging layer emits an explicit backpressure reason code to tracing (HEDGED_SHELF, EAGER_GRANT, SPILLED_FALLBACK) for postmortem and compensating actions
Config: per-tenant policy with rolling windows, max_shelf_rate, min_grant_floor, grace_ms, fallback_model_map
experiment_plan: Local simulator: replay production qps traces with synthetic KV-hotspot patterns (created from staging logs) to validate heuristics
Canary A/B: 10% of nodes run hedging controller (feature flag), 90% baseline. Run during non-peak and peak window for 72 hours each
Success metrics: reduce p999 latency on hedged nodes by >= 30% without decreasing median throughput by >1.5% and no increase in token cost >2%
Safety checks: enforced min_grant_floor to ensure high-priority tenants unaffected; circuit-breaker to disable hedging if GPU memutil crosses emergency threshold
test_plan: Unit test for quantile estimator and copula-based fusion logic
Load test in perf-cluster with controlled KV miss spikes and rapid tenant fanout
Chaos test: kill a gateway instance while hedged requests in shelf to validate retry semantics
Integration test: verify hedged metadata persists through to runtime allocator and is visible in tracing
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal perf runs in staging with real production traces (simulator) — target 1 week
Stage 1: Canary 10% nodes (feature flag) with monitoring alerts, 72h initial run
Stage 2: Expand to 30% if metrics stable for 72h and SLOs met
Stage 3: Global rollout with gradual ramp and automatic rollback if p999 degrades >5% vs baseline
decisions: Use probabilistic shelving (grace_ms) rather than immediate reject to improve median throughput under transient spikes
Implement estimator in Rust within gateway for low-latency signal fusion
No global KV locks; use lightweight request metadata to bias retention policies instead
Fallback path uses existing lower-cost compatible model variants rather than queueing indefinitely
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces extreme tails without heavy-handed KV eviction; preserves throughput and avoids GPU OOM by biased shedding

Cons: additional complexity in gateway and observability; slight increase in average request duration for shelved requests; potential fairness concerns for noisy tenants — mitigated by per-tenant policies and min_grant_floor
risks: Incorrect estimation under non-stationary traffic could over-shelf requests and hurt throughput
Edge case where shelf queue plus sudden grant flood overloads runtime — mitigated by slot-leak detection and emergency circuit-breaker
Telemetry cost increase from additional signals — quantify before wide rollout
